section_1.title: The Core Concept: Change Over Time
section_1.content: Define an ODE as an equation involving an unknown function and its derivatives. Introduce the intuition: while algebra solves for a 'value', ODEs solve for a 'behavior' or 'path'.
section_1.example: Visual of a squirrel jumping: The path is defined not just by its position, but by how its velocity changes (acceleration) relative to gravity.

section_2.title: Visualizing the Derivative: The Slope Field
section_2.content: Explain that an ODE gives a 'recipe' for the slope at any point. Visualize this as a 'vector field' or 'slope field'—a grid of tiny arrows representing the function's direction at that specific coordinate.
section_2.example: An animation showing a grid where arrows orient themselves; a particle follows the 'flow' of these arrows to trace out a smooth trajectory.

section_3.title: The First-Order ODE: Growth and Decay
section_3.content: Introduce the standard form dy/dx = ky. Explain that the rate of change is proportional to the current state. Prerequisite: Basic knowledge of exponential functions.
section_3.example: A population model of rabbits: The more rabbits there are (y), the faster the population grows (dy/dx). Show the graph curving upward exponentially.

section_4.title: Initial Conditions: Pinning Down the Solution
section_4.content: Explain that an ODE describes a family of curves (general solution). To find one specific curve, we need an 'Initial Condition' (where the object is at time t=0).
section_4.example: A robot arm starting its movement from a specific fixed point (x₀, y₀). The ODE defines all possible arm paths, but the initial condition picks the single trajectory the robot follows.

section_5.title: Summary & Real-World Synthesis
section_5.content: Brief recap: Model (ODE) + Starting Point (Initial Condition) = Predicted Future. Link the abstract symbols back to the real-world utility of predicting physical systems.
section_5.example: A rapid montage showing an ODE being solved to predict a falling ball, a heating cup of coffee, and a stock price fluctuation.
